$comment: Lighthouse CI configuration for the Splunk Monitoring Use Cases catalog. Consumed by .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml via the treosh/lighthouse-ci-action — same SHA pin policy as every other third-party action; verified by `python3 -m splunk_uc audit-action-pins`. The config targets the four highest-traffic pages of the static site: the UC explorer (index.html), the scorecard, the clause navigator, and one representative UC permalink (UC-1.1.1) chosen because it is the canonical example throughout AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. Thresholds are deliberately *warn-only* in this first cut — Lighthouse scores depend on CI runner load and Chrome version drift, so we collect a soak-period baseline before tightening any score floor into a hard gate. For that reason the assert block intentionally does NOT load an error-level preset (e.g. lighthouse:no-pwa): such presets inject dozens of per-audit assertions at *error* severity (color-contrast, errors-in-console, unused-javascript, unminified-css, unminified-javascript, unused-css-rules, cls-culprits-insight, …) which hard-fail the run and defeat the warn-only intent — that mismatch is what kept this workflow red on every push. We assert only the four category score floors, all at `warn`, so the job publishes trends without gating. To graduate into a hard gate after the soak period, add the specific audits you want to enforce here at `error` severity (or re-introduce a preset) and flip lighthouse.yml to a pull_request trigger. The collect.numberOfRuns: 1 setting keeps the workflow under 5 minutes; lift to 3 (the Lighthouse-CI default) once budgets stabilize and we want the trimmed-mean noise reduction.
